Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.intro: Memory Holder is a private diary. Here's everything it keeps, where that lives, and how to get rid of it. No small print.

what.title: What's stored
what.body:
Your account: email address, name, and password (encrypted — nobody can read it).
What you write: diaries, memories, dates, categories, and the photos and videos you upload.
Nothing else. No location, no contacts, no tracking of what you do on other sites.

where.title: Where it lives
where.body:
The database and the files are with Supabase, on servers in Singapore. The site itself runs on Vercel. Confirmation and password emails are sent through Resend.
Those three handle the data so the app can work. It isn't sold or passed on for anything else.

who.title: Who can see it
who.body:
Only the people in your diary. Each diary is walled off in the database: someone in another diary can't read your memories or open your photos, even with the link.
Whoever maintains the app has technical access to the database, as with any service. Nobody reads anyone's diary, but you should know it's possible.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body:
Only the ones the app can't work without: the one that keeps you signed in, the language you picked, which diary you're looking at, and light or dark mode.
There are no analytics or advertising cookies, and none from anyone else — which is why there's no cookie banner asking for permission.

keep.title: How long
keep.body:
For as long as you keep the account. Deleting a memory deletes its photos with it. Deleting your account removes everything of yours, and any diary only you were in goes too, photos included.
Diaries you share stay with the people still in them: those memories are theirs as well.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body:
You can delete your account whenever you like, from Admin panel → Account. No one to ask, nothing to wait for.
You can also ask for a copy of your data, have it corrected, or object to it being held, by writing to the address below.

Landing.heading: Your memories, somewhere that belongs only to you.
Landing.subheading: A shared diary of photos and the days worth keeping. You write it between you, and nobody else sees it.

timeline.title: A timeline
timeline.body: Every memory is a point on the line. Run the cursor along it and the day opens up, photo and all.

roulette.title: A roulette
roulette.body: Spin it when you can't decide what to remember, and it hands you back one of your own days.

categories.title: Categories
categories.body: Trips, firsts, Tuesday dinners — whichever ones you want, each with its own colour.

Landing.privateBody: Only the people you hand the code to get in. There's no public wall, no profiles, no ads and no tracking. Photos are served to the people in the diary and nobody else, and you can delete your account, and everything in it, in two clicks.
